newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-COLUMBUS WINS TWICE TO MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLUMBUS WINS TWICE TO MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE.

text.p: The Columbus Crew recorded a pair of shutout wins this weekend to move from fourth to first place in the Eastern Conference of Major League Soccer.

On Friday, the Crew (6-2) blanked the New England Revolution (4-3) in Foxboro, Massachusetts, 2-0, as Marcelo Carrera scored in the opening half and Jorge Salcedo added an insurance goal in the second half. On Sunday, the Crew continued its solid defensive play with a 3-0 triumph over the last-place New York/New Jersey MetroStars at home.
South African Doctor Khumalo, Carrera and Brian Maisonneuve scored for the Crew. U.S. international goalkeeper Brad Friedel recorded both shutouts.
Former U.S. World Cup captain and goalkeeper Tony Meola was used as a forward for the final 17 minutes for the goal-hungry MetroStars (3-6), who were shut out for the third consecutive match.

The MetroStars, directed by 1994 World Cup championship coach Carlos Alberto Parreira of Brazil, dropped a 1-0 decision to the San Jose Clash (4-4) in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Friday. Lawrence Lozzano scored his first goal of the season and former Italian international Roberto Donadoni missed a penalty kick in the 68th minute for the home team.
Steve Ralston scored his second goal of the game with four seconds remaining in regulation to lift the Tampa Bay Mutiny (5-2) to a 2-1 victory over the Colorado Rapids (3-6) in Tampa.

Ralston, last year's rookie of the year, scored off a through ball from Colombian international Carlos Valderrama, who also assisted on the midfielder's tying goal in the 71st minute. Former U.S. National Team defender Steve Trittschuh scored for the Rapids.
The Dallas Burn (5-4) recorded its second consecutive shootout win over defending champion D.C. United (5-3), registering a 3-2 victory after prevailing in the shootout, 2-1, in Washington, D.C.

Dallas goalkeeper Mark Dodd made three saves in the tie-breaker, on Bolivians Marco Etcheverry and Jaime Moreno and Honduran Arnold Cruz. Ted Eck and Peter Hattrup converted their chances for the Burn, who forced overtime on Jason Kreis' penalty kick in the 88th minute. Dante Washington scored two minutes into the match.
El Salvadoran striker Raul Diaz Arce and defender Eddie Pope, one of the heroes of last season's championship game, had goals for United.

Preki's goal in the 20th minute boosted the Kansas City Wizards (4-3) to a 1-0 win over the slumping Los Angeles Galaxy (1-7) and into first place in the Western Conference in Kansas City, Mo. The Galaxy, who have lost four straight games, took only one shot on goal -- by Danny Pena in the third minute. Goalkeeper Mike Ammannn recorded the shutout.
